decisions: QueueTransport, WorkerClock, QueueHandler, and DeadLetterSink are injected boundaries, so focused tests use fakes and never connect to Azure.
A message is deleted only after the idempotent handler completes successfully; handler failures below the limit leave the leased message for normal visibility-timeout retry.
The renewal loop carries forward Azure's updated pop receipt. On the final failed attempt, the worker sends to the injected dead-letter boundary before deleting the source message.

Duplicate deliveries are intentionally processed at least once. The injected handler owns deterministic object and catalog replacement, which makes restart and duplicate delivery safe without process-local deduplication.
limitations: Dead-letter transfer and source deletion are separate queue operations; a sink must be durable and idempotent because a crash between them can cause a repeated dead-letter transfer.
No live Azure, provider, credentials, network access, or MyPy run was used.
